entities.id: Geopolitical event as an external check
entities.description: Geopolitical disruptions – wars, sanctions, elections, contract breaches – act as external checks on prevailing market expectations. They are structurally unpredictable in terms of time, but can be analytically understood using Beckmann logic: one wonders which prevailing market expectation is most fragile if geopolitical stability is interrupted. The Russian invasion of Ukraine in 2022 is an example: the expectations of the European energy market were set on stable gas supplies for decades - external control was violent and rapid.

Act against the prevailing market expectation if the prerequisite analysis determines that this expectation is excessive. No reflexive contrarianism - logic requires evidence of dominance saturation, not mere disagreement. In Beckmann's words: The opposite position is the non-dominant expectation that undergoes a double reversal and appears as a linear fulfillment. Risk: Being too early is structurally identical to making a mistake in terms of loss of capital.

A market-shaping story—“the AI ​​revolution,” “the housing crisis,” “the commodities supercycle”—that is so widely accepted that it functions as an invisible premise rather than a thesis to be tested. Narrative dominance is dangerous precisely because it is no longer perceived as an expectation but as a reality. Presupposition analysis aims precisely at this transition point. When a narrative is no longer challenged, it is most vulnerable to reversal.

The market condition that arises after a reversal event dissolves the prevailing expectation. This is not a return to a previous state, but a truly new configuration: new dominant sectors, new evaluation frameworks, new dominant actors. Beckmann logic emphasizes that this new actual level immediately begins to form its own prevailing expectations - the cycle begins again. Investors who view the post-reversal state as stable are already building up the next low-complexity error.

The process by which market analysis is not a neutral observation but an active intervention in the system it describes. An analysis that reaches a large audience changes the dominant expectation vector of that audience, which in turn changes the pricing reality that the analysis describes. First systematized by George Soros. Expanded here by Beckmann logic: Reflexivity is a special case of self-inclusion in which the observer is structurally part of the observed system.

The danger that increases with the reach of a market analysis. A private conclusion has a negligible reflexive effect. The same conclusion published by Goldman Sachs, Bloomberg or a viral financial influencer changes the dominant expectation vector of millions of actors simultaneously. The higher the reach, the higher the likelihood that the analysis itself will become the main cause of the predicted market movement - and thus trigger a reversal effect.

The practice of explicitly incorporating the market implications of one's analysis or decision into the analysis itself. A low complexity analysis ignores its own influence. A highly complex analysis asks: How many people will see this conclusion? What will they do? How does this change the outcome I predict? Self-inclusion does not guarantee correct predictions, but it does prevent the systematic error of treating one's model as external to the system.

The irreducible uncertainty about when a correctly identified reversal condition will actually manifest itself in a price movement. Beckmann logic does not dissolve this limit - it explicitly recognizes it. A market thesis can be structurally correct (the prevailing expectation is untenable) but operationally useless if the timing is off by 18 months. Position sizing and risk management must take this uncertainty into account and must not eliminate it.

A sequential process of diffusion in which a prevailing expectation spreads across institutional layers - from leadership to middle management to the operational level, or from an institutional body to dependent bodies - and is reinforced at each stage by authority and formal confirmation. Each institutional level that adopts the prevailing expectation increases legitimacy, effectively increasing the calibration weight of the expectation and reducing the likelihood that lower levels will initiate a reverse diagnosis. Cascades differ from simple social diffusion in that they use institutional authority and resource allocation as reinforcement mechanisms, rather than just social conformity.

A social or institutional mechanism that systematically increases the strength and persistence of a dominant group expectation, thereby raising the threshold required to trigger a collective reversal. Amplifiers of social reversal include narrative reinforcement, institutional support, resource provision, and public explanation—each of which increases the cost of expectation revision and the social penalty for dissent. Unlike individual-level reverse reinforcers such as sunk costs, social reinforcers derive their power from collective coordination and the expectation of a coordinated response.

During the transitions of the collective expectation phase, the social reversal reinforcers that previously reinforced the prevailing expectation reverse their polarity and begin to reinforce the search for a new expectation, resulting in a rapid collective reversal. The transition represents the group-level analogue of the individual expectation reversal, but with higher thresholds, longer latencies, and a more abrupt onset.

entities.type: Transition of the collective expectation phase
entities.description: The minimum aggregate prediction error – summed across group members or institutional signals – required to initiate a transition of the collective expectation phase. The collective reversal threshold is higher than the average individual reversal threshold because social conformity pressure mechanisms and social reversal amplifiers filter out individual reversal signals before they aggregate. The threshold is modulated by the strength of the dominant group expectation, the degree of institutional commitment, and the presence or absence of collective security posture practices that maintain calibration.

A condition in which an institution receives sufficient prediction error signals to initiate an expectations revision, but is unable to complete the correction because institutional lock-in dynamics, social reversal reinforcers, and authority-based cascade mechanisms suppress the reversal process. The failure of an institutional correction is the analogue of the individual's calcification of expectations at the group level and results in the prevailing expectation remaining until an external social tipping trigger forces a transition in the collective expectation phase - typically at a much higher cost than previous voluntary corrections would have required. The failure of the correction is a leading indicator of an impending collective trend reversal on a large scale.

A publicly visible indicator that a group or institution is operating within a collective security situation - such as the presence of active channels for dissent, regular external scenario testing, or the explicit recognition of the uncertainty of expectations in official communication. Group-level safety signals calibrate the prevailing group expectation by signaling that the institution is not fully committed to the dominant prediction, thereby reducing the social penalty for individual expectation revision and lowering the collective reversal threshold. The absence of safety signals is a diagnostic indicator of increased risk of institutional corrective failure.

The group-level causal process by which shared prevailing expectations produce a reversal effect that spreads to multiple individuals simultaneously through social synchronization. Unlike individual reversal trajectories, this mechanism is reinforced by mutual reinforcement between actors, making the collective reversal faster, more severe, and more difficult to interrupt once initiated. It explains why reversal effects in social systems are disproportionately destructive compared to individual cases.

The process by which individual expectations within a group converge into a single dominant expectation through social feedback loops, communication cascades, and shared reference points. Through synchronization, the collective dominance ratio increases faster than the expectations of an individual alone could change. Once synchronization is complete, the group is maximally vulnerable to collective reversal because no internal divergent expectation can break the cascade.

The single agent causal path through which a person's internally prevailing expectation produces a reversal effect when real-world outcomes contradict it. The individual path is determined by the cognitive load at the moment of contradiction, the prior investment in the prevailing expectation and the availability of alternative explanatory frameworks. Unlike collective reversals, individual reversals can be interrupted by private reassessment before social propagation reinforces the effect.

The specific event, signal or piece of information whose arrival in a saturated expectation system causes the threshold to be crossed and the reversal sequence to begin. The trigger itself does not have to be large - its effect is disproportionate since the system is already in a warning state before the reversal. Understanding trigger events allows for earlier identification of what constitutes a dangerous disconfirmation signal within a specific range of expectations.

The self-sustaining impulse of a reversal effect after the threshold has been crossed, which maintains and reinforces the reversed expectation orientation even after the original trigger has passed. Inertia is driven by the dynamics of sunk costs, narrative reinterpretations, and societal pressures to conform to the newly prevailing reverse expectation. It explains why reversal effects persist and deepen rather than correcting themselves once triggered, and why early intervention before the threshold is crossed is far more effective than correction after the reversal.

relations.subject: Wigner's friend

relations.subject: Superposition

relations.subject: Decoherence

She explains why the brain does not perceive superpositions in everyday life and instead receives a stable, classic 3D world model without solving the collapse itself.

relations.subject: Measurement problem / collapse of the wave function

Decoherence explains the transition from quantum probabilities to classical probabilities, but leaves open why exactly this one result appears in the consciousness of the observer.

relations.subject: Wave function

It contains complete information about possible measurement outputs and is the raw data structure of the outside world from which the brain extracts a clear 3D world model using decoherence.

relations.subject: Quantum field theory and vacuum fluctuation

Vacuum fluctuations show that even the vacuum is not nothing, but has a complex structure of field wave functions that the 3D world model renders as empty.

relations.subject: Quantum Predictive Brain

To do this, it uses the mathematics of quantum mechanics with Hilbert space, superposition and non-commutative operators as a formalism to model cognitive phenomena such as sequence effects, cognitive dissonance and contextuality, which are difficult to render classically. It's not about quantum physics in the brain, but about quantum mathematics as a logic model.

relations.subject: Predictive Brain Theory

It is the direct conceptual basis for the Quantum Predictive Brain, which retains the same prediction mechanism but replaces classical probability logic with quantum probability logic to better explain the cognitive biases observed in the 3D world model.

relations.subject: balance effect

relations.subject: Wigner's friend

The friend in the laboratory experiences a defined collapse, while Wigner describes the entire laboratory including the friend as a superposition. It shows that the question of when and by whom a 3D world model is established remains unanswered within standard quantum mechanics.

relations.subject: Quantum Predictive Brain

While Quantum Brain claims that the brain performs physically real quantum computations in microtubules and requires objective collapse, Quantum Predictive Brain uses quantum mechanics only as the mathematics of cognition. It is a purely information-theoretic and functional level of description of the human logic model, without postulating speculative quantum biology in the brain.

relations.subject: Quantum effects in biology

They thus provide the possible empirical basis for the quantum brain hypothesis, which assumes that the human brain also exploits non-trivial quantum effects for consciousness, even if the transfer to neuronal structures remains speculative.

Experimental signature according to the article: Sinusoidal subthreshold oscillation with scattering hbar²/4 around classical cosine. Clear, testable prediction.

relations.description: The spread of subthreshold oscillations around the classic cosine wave is hbar/4. Measuring this scattering using high-resolution electrophysiological techniques (patch clamp) allows direct determination of hbar. Thermodynamic properties approach zero point energy at T→0.

relations.subject: Neural constant hbar = m sigma
relations.object: Empirical determination of hbar via variance and inductance
relations.description: hbar is empirically determined by (a) variance of membrane potential q=C V: sigma² = Var(q)/Δt and (b) inductance m=L from LCR circuit adjustment of subthreshold oscillations or piezoelectric equivalent inductance through myelin. Early measurements on the squid giant axon showed small L, myelin-containing mammalian neurons could have large effective inductance and therefore large audibility.

relations.subject: Stochastic FitzHugh-Nagumo model with quantum correction
relations.description: Unlike Quantum Brain (Penrose-Hameroff Orch-OR), which postulates true quantum computations in microtubules, protected by Debye layers and actin gel, and assumes objective gravitational collapse, the stochastic FN model does not require quantum physics in the brain. It only uses quantum-like mathematics as a level of description for classical Brownian noise. Not a quantum computer, but a classical system with a hidden Schroedinger structure.

relations.subject: Quantum Predictive Brain
relations.object: Stochastic FitzHugh-Nagumo model with quantum correction
relations.description: Quantum Predictive Brain replaces classical Bayesian inference with quantum probability to model cognitive order effects. The FN result provides possible biophysical realization: If neuronal membrane dynamics are already Schroedinger-like, the brain could naturally implement quantum-like logic without being a quantum computer. Connects abstract QPB logic with concrete ion channel dynamics and suggests that entanglement-like correlations may occur between neurons via Nelson mapping.

relations.subject: Human brain
relations.object: Quantum-like coherence through noise – Order from Disorder
relations.description: The human brain as biological hardware with approximately 20W generates quantum-like coherence in its electromagnetic field despite massive decoherence at the molecular level by using thermal, mechanical and synaptic noise. Stochastic processes in neuronal membranes, modeled as Brownian motion, have hidden phase S and amplitude sqrt(rho), which can interfere. This could provide new insights into mechanisms of brain function and consciousness.

relations.subject: Dark matter in the cosmic microwave background radiation
relations.description: The observed anisotropies of the cosmic microwave background radiation are consistent with a significant non-baryonic matter component and provide evidence for the dark matter phenomenon that is independent of galaxy dynamics.

relations.subject: Dark matter as a form of matter
relations.description: In the standard model of cosmology, the hypothetical dark matter component is modeled as cold matter, which is non-relativistic in the relevant structure formation.

relations.subject: Cold Dark Matter
relations.description: In the Cold Dark Matter model, dark matter forms large-scale halo structures in which galaxies are embedded.

relations.subject: Lambda CDM model
relations.description: Cold dark matter is a central matter component of the Lambda-CDM model.

relations.subject: Group dominance patterns
relations.description: The group dominance pattern provides the raw synchronized state of expectation that institutional expectation cascades then propagate and reinforce through formal authority structures. Without a stable group dominance pattern as input, the cascade has no dominant expectation to support institutionally, so the cascade mechanism is downstream of the synchronization of expectations at the group level.

relations.subject: collective_expectation anchor
relations.description: Collective expectation anchors prevent the group dominance pattern from unraveling in the event of minor prediction errors by providing a common historical or narrative reference that redefines disconfirmatory signals as anomalies rather than true reversal triggers. The anchor increases the calibration weight of the dominant expectation and thus the threshold at which the group initiates expectation search.

relations.subject: social_conformity pressure mechanism
relations.description: Mechanisms of social conformity pressure increase the collective reversal threshold by suppressing individual deviant prediction signals before they can aggregate into a group-level prediction error. Each individual who conforms increases the apparent consensus strength of the prevailing expectation and requires a proportionately larger external signal to cross the threshold.

relations.subject: social_reversal_amplifier
relations.description: Social reverse amplifiers increase the speed and depth of institutional expectation cascades by adding social enforcement mechanisms—narrative conformity, reputational pressure, resource allocation—on top of the authority-based spread of the cascade. Strong amplifiers transform a slow cascade into a rapid lock-in dynamic that reaches all institutional levels before a single level can initiate a correction.

relations.subject: institutional_expectation cascade
relations.description: As an institutional expectation cascade spreads across successive institutional levels, the formal endorsement of each level commits resources and reputational capital to the prevailing expectation, thereby gradually creating the conditions for institutional commitment. The cascade is the generative process; Lock-in is the stable state it creates once the cascade has reached sufficient institutional depth.

relations.subject: institutional_lock_in_the_dynamic
relations.description: Institutional lock-in dynamics lead to corrective errors by making expectation revision structurally costly: The sunk obligations encoded in the lock-in state mean that recognition of a dominant expectation error triggers resource write-offs, reputational damage, and leadership responsibilities that exceed the expected costs of maintaining the erroneous prediction. This asymmetry prevents correction even when prediction error signals are clearly visible.

relations.subject: Trigger for social tipping point
relations.description: A social tipping point trigger initiates the transition of the collective expectation phase by providing a prediction error signal that exceeds the collective reversal threshold and cannot be assimilated by existing reframing mechanisms. The trigger transforms the accumulated prediction error - previously suppressed by social reinforcers - into a visible and publicly acknowledged collapse of expectations and catalyzes the phase transition.

relations.subject: collective_reversal_threshold
relations.description: The collective reversal threshold determines at which point the accumulated prediction error produces a phase transition from continued maintenance of the dominant expectation. Understanding the threshold makes it possible to distinguish between stable dominant expectancy states, pre-transition accumulation states, and the beginning of the phase transition - a distinction that is central to predicting the timing and extent of collective reversal.

relations.subject: collective_security posture
relations.description: A collective safety posture lowers the collective reversal threshold by maintaining active channels for divergent predictions and regular external calibration, meaning prediction errors emerge earlier and aggregate. Groups with strong collective security positions initiate expectation phase transitions at smaller prediction error sizes, resulting in smaller reversals at higher frequencies rather than large reversals at low frequencies.

relations.subject: collective_security posture
relations.description: Y7's collective security situation operationalizes the very structural conditions that prevent institutional corrections from failing: mandatory channels for dissent, adversarial scrutiny, and recognition of uncertainty each remove the social and structural barriers that cause corrections to fail. The presence of a collective security situation is the most reliable indicator of whether an institution is self-correcting before an external tip or whether a complete transition to the collective expectation phase is required.

relations.subject: institutional_corrective failure
relations.description: Institutional corrective failure reinforces and deepens the group dominance pattern by signaling to group members that the dominant expectation has been tested and has survived the test, even if that survival was brought about by repression rather than confirmation. Each failed correction attempt increases the apparent calibration value of the dominant expectation, thereby strengthening the group dominance pattern for the next cycle.

relations.subject: Security_signal_at_group_level
relations.description: Security signals at the Y7 group level are the visible expression of collective security commitments - they make the institution's expectation calibration practices publicly visible and socially credible. Without security signals, a collective security posture remains private and does not reduce the social penalty for individual expectation revision, which limits its threshold-lowering function.

relations.subject: Security_signal_at_group_level
relations.description: The presence or absence of group-level safety signals is a diagnostic indicator that distinguishes institutions at risk of corrective error from those operating with active expectation calibration. The lack of publicly visible safety signals suggests an increased risk of correction error because it shows that there is no structural possibility for different predictions within the institutional expectation cascade.

relations.subject: social_conformity pressure mechanism
relations.description: Social conformity pressure mechanisms are the primary implementation mechanism through which social reversal reinforcers achieve their threshold-raising effect: conformity pressure transforms the suppression of individual expectations into an aggregate reinforcement of the dominant group's prediction, thus producing the reinforcer's characteristic increase in the reinforcer's dominant expectancy strength without new external evidence.

relations.subject: Synchronization_of_group_expectations
relations.description: The synchronization of individual expectations within a group increases the collective dominance ratio to threshold levels and thus creates the conditions for a reversal at the group level. Without synchronization, individual reversals remain isolated and do not lead to collective effects.

relations.subject: Cascade_of_social_reinforcement
relations.description: The amplification cascade accelerates the synchronization speed and suppresses divergent expectations. It determines how quickly a group moves from distributed expectations to dangerous convergence. A higher cascade intensity shortens the time available for intervention at the warning level.

relations.subject: cognitive_load_at_the_threshold
relations.description: The cognitive load at the moment of the contradiction determines whether the person can perform a corrective reappraisal or whether the contradiction is processed as a trigger for a complete reversal. A high load eliminates the possibility of self-interruption and makes the single path deterministic once the threshold is exceeded.

relations.subject: individual_expectations
relations.description: The trajectory operationalizes the individual reversal mechanism by providing the temporal sequence through which anchoring is established - demonstrating that the mechanism is not instantaneous, but a gradual process whose outcome can be influenced at certain earlier points.

relations.subject: collective_reversal mechanism
relations.description: A fully synchronized collective in warning stage saturation requires only a minimal trigger event to exceed the threshold, while the collective mechanism itself generates the structural reinforcement that makes small triggers catastrophically effective.

relations.subject: individual_reversal mechanism
relations.description: At the individual level, the triggering reversal event is the specific information input that exceeds the individual's threshold - calibrated by cognitive load and trajectory - and produces the reversal sequence in the single agent pathway.

relations.subject: Reversal trigger event
relations.description: Once the triggering event crosses the threshold and initiates a reversal, the inertia mechanism takes over and maintains the reversed expectation orientation through sunk cost dynamics and narrative reinterpretation, preventing self-correction even after the trigger signal has passed.

relations.subject: Pre-reversal warning level
relations.description: The warning phase defines the structural context in which a specific event becomes a trigger. A distinction is made between whether the same event is irrelevant in a system with low saturation and whether it is catastrophic in a system before the reversal at the threshold. This differentiation makes trigger identification domain-sensitive and context-dependent and not event-universal.

relations.subject: Inertia_after_the_reversal
relations.description: Inertia affects the threshold model by showing that the model must take hysteresis into account - the threshold for recovery after a complete reversal is significantly higher than the threshold for preventing such a reversal, which affects the future calibration of the warning level limits.
